summary: 1940 Aermotor LS-40 fire tower in Mitchell County, Georgia, run by the Georgia Forestry Commission; the Register says it is still occasionally manned.

facts.design: 80-foot Aermotor LS-40 galvanized steel tower with 7-by-7-foot cab

staffing.status: occasionally manned; part-time forestry station at its base (Register description)

access.note: The Register gives no visiting terms. It lists the Georgia Forestry Commission's Flint District as cooperator; the description places a part-time operational forestry station at the tower's base.

events.note: Register Built field gives 1940; its description says built between 1935 and 1940
Register description: still occasionally manned, with a part-time operational forestry station at its base; date is the registration year, not a staffing log

evidence.supports: administered by the Georgia Forestry Commission
built between 1935 and 1940; 80-foot Aermotor LS-40 galvanized steel tower with 7x7 cab; occasionally manned; part-time forestry station at base
evidence.quote: Built between 1935 and 1940, this 80' Aermotor LS-40 galvanized steel tower with 7'x7' cab is one of 20 or 30 firetowers in Georgia that are still occasionally manned, with a part time operational forestry station at its base.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Built field gives 1940; the description says built between 1935 and 1940. The event uses 1940 and keeps the range in its note.

photos.caption: Newton lookout tower, GA37 Mitchell County, Georgia

notes_for_editor: One source (the NHLR page). Height converted from the Register's 80 ft to 24.4 m; the Register does not give metres for the tower itself. Staffing date is the 2013 registration, not a dated staffing report. No fire history or later condition report found. Photo is from Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0, not checked against the image itself. Brief's access 'unknown' kept as unknown.
